network_thesis.headline: Caribbean Mobility Partner × Navier — one app for island-to-island premium movement
network_thesis.body: A generic Caribbean mobility partner should not be a fake ride-hail footprint. It is a regional operating proposal for a partner that can aggregate airport, resort, marina, ferry, taxi, and concierge demand across island markets where Atlas already has geometry. The Grab gold standard becomes: broad regional thesis first, exact Atlas binding second, economics only where demand/country references are sourced.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Start with display-ready Atlas markets; promote only as evidence and economics gates pass.

partner_context.their_ambition: A Caribbean mobility aggregator can become the premium travel layer across fragmented island transport: airport arrivals, resort transfers, cruise/marina movements, inter-island day trips, and on-island last mile.
partner_context.their_pressure: The region is high-value but operationally fragmented: separate taxi systems, ferry timetables, resort shuttles, cruise peaks, and island-by-island regulation.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier becomes the water leg inside a door-to-door Caribbean trip stack. The partner sells the journey; Navier operates the efficient foiling marine layer.

hero.title: Caribbean Mobility Partner × Navier — one app for island-to-island premium movement
hero.subtitle: Build from existing Atlas Caribbean geometry; do not invent partner city coverage or route economics until each corridor has anchors.
hero.what_we_do_together: We package a regional premium-water mobility layer for the Caribbean: Bahamas, Puerto Rico/Spanish Virgins, USVI/BVI, Barbados, Jamaica, Dominican Republic, St Lucia/Grenadines, Turks & Caicos, Cayman, Antigua, and ABC islands. The proposal is intentionally partner-generic until an operator is chosen; the geography is Atlas-grounded, the operating model is partner-ready, and the gaps are explicit.

why_now: Caribbean travel has recovered into a high-value tourism and investment cycle, while climate resilience and sustainable transport are now central policy themes. Uber's Barbados launch shows app-based mobility entering Eastern Caribbean tourist markets, but water remains the unbundled premium layer.

why_navier_now.step_change: Navier can make short island, marina, resort, and cruise-port hops feel like premium mobility rather than ferry logistics. Range gates keep N30/N35 on short commercial legs and reserve longer inter-island ambitions for Quanta-LR.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Uses existing waterways, marinas, ports, and app dispatch rather than new right-of-way.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Caribbean travel has recovered into a high-value tourism and investment cycle, while climate resilience and sustainable transport are now central policy themes. Uber's Barbados launch shows app-based mobility entering Eastern Caribbean tourist markets, but water remains the unbundled premium layer.

multimodal_fit: The partner coordinates pickup, luggage/concierge, marina handoff, water transfer, and arrival ride. Navier contributes the vessel, route operating model, and clean premium experience.

differentiation.headline: Exactness over coverage
differentiation.body: This is an operator-ready regional proposal, not a false claim that one partner already operates everywhere. Existing Atlas geometry gates display; country-reference/demand-anchor preflight gates economics. Markets are split into display-ready, inherited/brief-only, and true gaps before Grok seals anything.

proof_points: Existing Atlas Caribbean nodes found in data-clean: Nassau/Bahamas, Puerto Rico, USVI/BVI, Barbados, Jamaica, Samaná/Dominican Republic, St Lucia/Grenadines, Turks & Caicos, Cayman, Antigua, ABC islands.
Uber Barbados 2025 launch: Uber Taxi officially available across Barbados and first Eastern Caribbean launch.
Tourism Analytics: Caribbean tourism data platform covering 33+ destinations / 40+ destinations language on site.
OECD Caribbean Development Dynamics 2026: region requires faster and higher-quality investment amid climate risks and structural vulnerabilities.

objections.objection: There is no named Caribbean platform partner yet.
objections.response: Correct. This is a generic mobility-partner blueprint with exact market readiness; once a partner is named, only the partner footprint/evidence layer changes.

objections.objection: Country refs are missing for many Caribbean markets.
objections.response: Do not run final economics until country-reference rows and demand anchors are added. The gap queue names that explicitly.

objections.objection: Inter-island routes can exceed N30 range or trigger customs/regulatory complexity.
objections.response: Use short commercial-now routes first; mark long/cross-border routes as Quanta-LR or authority-dependent roadmap.

objections.objection: Tourism volume does not equal water demand.
objections.response: Correct; tourism sources prioritize markets, but corridor economics need route-specific ferry/visitor/airport/resort demand anchors before gold economics.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $1M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM — floor (published)
rungs.basis: sourced flagship corridors · 10% capture · today's demand

rungs.label: SOM — full network
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 10% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.label: SAM — matured network
rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

rungs.label: Marine mobility TAM — induced marine-transfer market
rungs.basis: SAM divided by leading-operator capture — the full inducible water-transfer wallet at network maturity

rungs.label: Journey GMV — food + stays + experiences (≈3× TAM)
rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

rungs.label: Partner platform revenue on Navier
rungs.basis: platform commission on journey GMV routed through the Navier network (subset of full Journey GMV)

ceiling_sibling.label: Platform revenue ceiling — 18% × full Journey GMV
ceiling_sibling.derivation: journey_gmv.mid × 0.18 (full GMV ceiling, not Navier-corridor subset)
ceiling_sibling._doc: Sibling reference. Do NOT promote to a 7th ladder rung. Platform_rev rung remains the Navier-subset Interpretation-A value.

phase_economics.headline: Revenue potential by phase — conservative floor first, ecosystem prize last.
phase_economics.conversion_note: Fleet & CO2 scale from the grounded unit: 1 boats = $0M transport rev = 8 t CO2/yr (~$119K rev/boat).

horizons.name: Prove
horizons.vessel: N30 Pioneer II (8 pax, commercial now)

horizons.name: Scale
horizons.scope: Extend to the full mapped greenfield network
horizons.vessel: N30 Pioneer II + N35 Shuttle (12–15 pax, 2027) on dense legs

horizons.name: Mature
horizons.scope: Induced marine-transfer demand + leading-operator capture across the network
horizons.vessel: N35-led mix; Quanta-LR on 75–150nm regional legs (H2 2026+)
horizons.fleet_note: Pioneer-equivalent; N35 mix lowers hull count for the same throughput.

vessel_sizing.headline: Right vessel for every leg — corridor range picks the hull.

classes.role: Capillary corridors ≤ 70nm. The workhorse of Prove + Scale.
Doubles throughput per hull on dense corridors; roughly halves payback. Scale-phase workhorse.
Regional legs 75–150nm beyond Pioneer range. Held out of near-term numbers.

vessel_sizing.range_gate_note: ≤ 70nm → Pioneer II (now). 75–150nm → Quanta-LR (roadmap). Long legs never faked on a 70nm boat.

_render_chip_flag.confidence_display: Tag every banded rung; lead with floor + corridor COUNT (ID-traceable). Never headline the 'high' band.

growth_case.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
growth_case.modal_headline: Floor to prize — every rung traces to grounded demand

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.headline: Caribbean-Mobility platform take on Navier-carried journeys
ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).
ladder_transitions._lb_ref: LB-113: partner_platform_rev_on_navier = on-Navier subset, distinct from deck's '18% × full Journey GMV' narrative ceiling

_retire_note: Lumped aruba-curacao-bonaire market superseded by caribbean + ocean-whisperer ABC seal (PR #93).
